weldability_notes: No preheat. Use ER316L filler. Low carbon prevents sensitization.
typical_applications: Marine hardware, chemical processing equipment, pharmaceutical tanks, food processing, medical implants.
key_warnings: Sensitization risk between 425-850 deg C. Galvanic corrosion with carbon steel. Not for high-temp oxidation above 870 deg C.
sources: ASME BPVC II-D Table 1A Line 34|Shigley A-22|Cardarelli §1.1.4|Outokumpu Acom 4-2007
description_text: 316L Stainless Steel is a stainless austenitic with a yield strength of 170 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: Marine hardware, chemical processing equipment, pharmaceutical tanks, food processing, medical implants. Key engineering considerations: Sensitization risk between 425-850 deg C. Galvanic corrosion with carbon steel. Not for high-temp oxidation above 870 deg C.

weldability_notes: No preheat. Use ER308L filler. Low carbon prevents weld decay.
typical_applications: Food processing, brewery and dairy tanks, architectural trim, kitchen sinks, chemical storage.
key_warnings: Less corrosion-resistant than 316L in chlorides. Sensitization minimized by low carbon. Galvanic risk with carbon steel.
sources: ASME BPVC II-D Table 1A Line 30|Shigley A-22|Cardarelli §1.1|Outokumpu Acom 4-2007
description_text: 304L Stainless Steel is a stainless austenitic with a yield strength of 170 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: Food processing, brewery and dairy tanks, architectural trim, kitchen sinks, chemical storage. Key engineering considerations: Less corrosion-resistant than 316L in chlorides. Sensitization minimized by low carbon. Galvanic risk with carbon steel.

weldability_notes: Welding not recommended due to sulfur hot cracking. If required, use ER312 filler with low heat input.
typical_applications: Screw machine parts, fittings, fasteners, shafts, bushings, nuts, valve components.
key_warnings: Sulfur reduces corrosion resistance vs 304/304L. Poor weldability. Not for marine. Reduced transverse ductility.
description_text: 303 Stainless Steel (Free-Machining) is a stainless austenitic with a yield strength of 241 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is fair (2/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Screw machine parts, fittings, fasteners, shafts, bushings, nuts, valve components. Key engineering considerations: Sulfur reduces corrosion resistance vs 304/304L. Poor weldability. Not for marine. Reduced transverse ductility.

weldability_notes: No preheat. Use ER308L filler. Standard austenitic weldability.
typical_applications: Chemical and food processing equipment, brewing equipment, cryogenic vessels, gutters, downspouts, flashings.
key_warnings: Less corrosion-resistant than 316 in chlorides. Use 304L for welded fabrication to avoid sensitization. Galvanic risk with carbon steel.
description_text: 304 Stainless Steel is a stainless austenitic with a yield strength of 255 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: Chemical and food processing equipment, brewing equipment, cryogenic vessels, gutters, downspouts, flashings. Key engineering considerations: Less corrosion-resistant than 316 in chlorides. Use 304L for welded fabrication to avoid sensitization. Galvanic risk with carbon steel.

weldability_notes: No preheat. Use ER316L filler.
typical_applications: High corrosion resistance and high creep strength. Chemical and pulp-handling equipment, photographic equipment, fertilizer parts, ketchup-cooking kettles, yeast tubs.
key_warnings: Sensitization between 425-850 deg C - prefer 316L for welded applications. Galvanic corrosion with carbon steel.
description_text: 316 Stainless Steel is a stainless austenitic with a yield strength of 250 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: High corrosion resistance and high creep strength. Chemical and pulp-handling equipment, photographic equipment, fertilizer parts. Key engineering considerations: Sensitization between 425-850 deg C - prefer 316L for welded applications.

weldability_notes: Preheat 200-300 C required. PWHT mandatory. Use ER410 filler. Crack-prone.
typical_applications: Cutlery blades, valve parts, pump shafts, turbine blades, mild service steam fittings.
key_warnings: Magnetic. Hardenable - useful for wear but increases brittleness. Lower corrosion resistance than austenitic grades. Tempering above 540 C causes embrittlement zone.
description_text: 410 Stainless Steel (Martensitic) is a stainless martensitic with a yield strength of 275 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is fair (2/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Cutlery blades, valve parts, pump shafts, turbine blades, mild service steam fittings. Key engineering considerations: Magnetic. Hardenable - useful for wear but increases brittleness. Lower corrosion resistance than austenitic grades. Tempering above 540 C causes embrittlement zone.

weldability_notes: Welding not recommended - sulfur causes hot cracking. Preheat 250 C if welding required.
typical_applications: Aircraft fittings, bolts, nuts, fire extinguisher inserts, rivets, screws - highest machinability martensitic stainless.
key_warnings: Sulfur addition for machinability severely reduces corrosion resistance and weldability. Not for marine. Must be heat-treated for hardness applications.
description_text: 416 Stainless Steel (Free-Machining Martensitic) is a stainless martensitic with a yield strength of 275 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is fair (2/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Aircraft fittings, bolts, nuts, fire extinguisher inserts, rivets, screws. Key engineering considerations: Sulfur addition for machinability severely reduces corrosion resistance and weldability. Not for marine. Must be heat-treated for hardness applications.

weldability_notes: Preheat 150-200 C. Use ER430 or ER309 filler. Grain growth at high temp reduces toughness.
typical_applications: Automotive trim, appliance panels, kitchen equipment, mild atmospheric exposure, decorative parts.
key_warnings: Magnetic. Cannot be hardened by heat treatment. Notch-sensitive at low temp. Less ductile than austenitic. SCC in specific conditions.
description_text: 430 Stainless Steel (Ferritic) is a stainless ferritic with a yield strength of 240 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is fair (2/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Automotive trim, appliance panels, kitchen equipment, mild atmospheric exposure, decorative parts. Key engineering considerations: Magnetic. Cannot be hardened by heat treatment. Notch-sensitive at low temp. Less ductile than austenitic. SCC in specific conditions.

weldability_notes: Weldable with care using ER630 filler. Solution treat and age after welding to restore properties.
typical_applications: Aerospace fittings, valve stems, pump shafts, high-strength corrosion-resistant fasteners, gas turbine parts.
key_warnings: Properties degrade above 315 C. SCC risk in marine. Cannot be re-hardened without full re-treatment. More brittle than austenitic stainless.
description_text: 17-4 PH Stainless Steel (H1025) is a stainless ph with a yield strength of 1000 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is moderate (3/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Aerospace fittings, valve stems, pump shafts, high-strength corrosion-resistant fasteners, gas turbine parts. Key engineering considerations: Properties degrade above 315 C. SCC risk in marine. Cannot be re-hardened without full re-treatment. More brittle than austenitic stainless.

weldability_notes: Excellent weldability. E6013 or E7018 electrodes. No preheat for most thicknesses.
typical_applications: Structural components, brackets, mounting plates, general fabrication, fixtures, low-stress shafts, bushings, hinges.
key_warnings: Rusts rapidly. Not for marine/chemical. Brittle below -30 C. Limited hardenability. Not for high-stress fatigue.
description_text: Carbon Steel 1018 (Hot-Rolled) is a carbon steel low with a yield strength of 220 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: Structural components, brackets, mounting plates, general fabrication, fixtures, low-stress shafts, bushings, hinges. Key engineering considerations: Rusts rapidly. Not for marine/chemical. Brittle below -30 C. Limited hardenability. Not for high-stress fatigue.

weldability_notes: Good weldability but cold-work near welds is annealed out. E7018 electrodes.
typical_applications: Precision shafts, machined parts, fasteners, hydraulic components, where tighter tolerances and better surface finish are needed.
key_warnings: Cold-drawn condition is lost in heat-affected zone after welding. Residual stresses may cause distortion during machining. Same corrosion issues as HR.
description_text: Carbon Steel 1018 (Cold-Drawn) is a carbon steel low with a yield strength of 370 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is good (4/5). Typical applications include: Precision shafts, machined parts, fasteners, hydraulic components, where tighter tolerances and better surface finish are needed. Key engineering considerations: Cold-drawn condition is lost in heat-affected zone after welding. Residual stresses may cause distortion during machining. Same corrosion issues as HR.

weldability_notes: Good weldability with E7018. Preheat 100-150 C for thick sections. PWHT recommended above 25mm.
typical_applications: Shafts, axles, gears, crankshafts, connecting rods, machine components.
key_warnings: Rusts rapidly. Not for marine/chemical. Brittle below -30 C. Surface decarburization possible.
description_text: Carbon Steel 1040 (Hot-Rolled) is a carbon steel medium with a yield strength of 290 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is good (4/5). Typical applications include: Shafts, axles, gears, crankshafts, connecting rods, machine components. Key engineering considerations: Rusts rapidly. Not for marine/chemical. Brittle below -30 C. Surface decarburization possible.

weldability_notes: Poor weldability - high carbon. Preheat 200-300 C. PWHT mandatory. Low-hydrogen electrodes only.
typical_applications: Cutting blades, springs, knives, wear plates, hammers, axes, leaf springs.
key_warnings: Welding difficult and risky. Cracking without PWHT. Loses temper above 425 C. Hydrogen embrittlement during plating.
description_text: Carbon Steel 1050 (Q&T at 425C) is a carbon steel high with a yield strength of 793 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Cutting blades, springs, knives, wear plates, hammers, axes, leaf springs. Key engineering considerations: Welding difficult and risky. Cracking without PWHT. Loses temper above 425 C. Hydrogen embrittlement during plating.

weldability_notes: Essentially not weldable due to very high carbon (0.95%). Mechanical joining only.
typical_applications: Knife blades, springs, cutting tools, files, leaf springs, music wire.
key_warnings: Cannot be welded. Must be heat-treated for application use (typically Q&T). Highest hardness ability of plain carbon steels. Brittle if over-hardened.
description_text: Carbon Steel 1095 (Annealed) is a carbon steel high with a yield strength of 460 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is poor (1/5). Typical applications include: Knife blades, springs, cutting tools, files, leaf springs, music wire. Key engineering considerations: Cannot be welded. Must be heat-treated for application use (typically Q&T). Highest hardness ability of plain carbon steels. Brittle if over-hardened.

weldability_notes: Excellent weldability. E7018 electrodes. No preheat for sections up to 25mm.
typical_applications: Structural beams, bridges, buildings, machinery frames, general fabrication - most common structural steel.
key_warnings: Rusts rapidly - protective coating required. Low hardenability. Not suitable for elevated temperature service without analysis. Brittle below -30 C.
description_text: HSLA Steel A36 (Structural) is a carbon steel low with a yield strength of 250 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: Structural beams, bridges, buildings, machinery frames, general fabrication. Key engineering considerations: Rusts rapidly - protective coating required. Low hardenability. Not suitable for elevated temperature service without analysis. Brittle below -30 C.

weldability_notes: Weldable with care. Preheat 150-200 C. PWHT recommended. Use ER80S-D2. Aerospace TIG welded.
typical_applications: Aerospace structural, motorcycle and bicycle frames, race car roll cages, aircraft tubing, high-strength shafts.
key_warnings: Used as 4140 substitute when better weldability needed. Hydrogen embrittlement during plating. SCC risk in chlorides.
description_text: Alloy Steel 4130 (Q&T at 540C) is an alloy steel with a yield strength of 910 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Aerospace structural, motorcycle and bicycle frames, race car roll cages, aircraft tubing, high-strength shafts. Key engineering considerations: Used as 4140 substitute when better weldability needed. Hydrogen embrittlement during plating. SCC risk in chlorides.

weldability_notes: Limited weldability. Preheat 300-400 C mandatory. PWHT essential. Low-hydrogen electrodes only.
typical_applications: High-strength shafts, gears, axles, crankshafts, bolts, drilling components, gun barrels, machine spindles.
key_warnings: Most common high-strength alloy steel. Poor weldability. Hydrogen embrittlement during electroplating. SCC in H2S environments.
description_text: Alloy Steel 4140 (Q&T at 540C) is an alloy steel with a yield strength of 834 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: High-strength shafts, gears, axles, crankshafts, bolts, drilling components, gun barrels, machine spindles. Key engineering considerations: Most common high-strength alloy steel. Poor weldability. Hydrogen embrittlement during electroplating. SCC in H2S environments.

weldability_notes: Poor weldability. Preheat 350-400 C. Strict PWHT required. Hydrogen control critical.
typical_applications: Aircraft landing gear, heavy-duty shafts, ordnance, high-stress forgings, gears under heavy load.
key_warnings: One of the highest hardenability steels. Hydrogen embrittlement extremely risky during plating - bake immediately. Very expensive vs 4140.
description_text: Alloy Steel 4340 (Q&T at 540C) is an alloy steel with a yield strength of 1080 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Aircraft landing gear, heavy-duty shafts, ordnance, high-stress forgings, gears under heavy load. Key engineering considerations: One of the highest hardenability steels. Hydrogen embrittlement extremely risky during plating - bake immediately. Very expensive vs 4140.

weldability_notes: Slightly better than Q&T 4140 for welding. Preheat 200-250 C. PWHT recommended.
typical_applications: Pre-machined stock that will be heat-treated later, large forgings where through-hardening is impractical, gear blanks.
key_warnings: Uniform grain structure but lower strength than Q&T. Often supplied normalized for further machining and final heat treatment by user.
description_text: Alloy Steel 4140 (Normalized) is an alloy steel with a yield strength of 655 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Pre-machined stock that will be heat-treated later, large forgings where through-hardening is impractical, gear blanks. Key engineering considerations: Uniform grain structure but lower strength than Q&T. Often supplied normalized for further machining and final heat treatment by user.

weldability_notes: Welding not normally done. If required, requires specialized procedures with intense preheat, controlled cooling, and full re-heat treatment.
typical_applications: Cold-work tooling, blanking dies, forming dies, slitter knives, thread rolling dies, shear blades, punches.
key_warnings: Brittle in hardened condition. Very low elongation - cannot deform. Must be machined before hardening. Susceptible to fracture under impact load.
description_text: Tool Steel D2 (Hardened & Tempered) is a tool steel with a yield strength of 1800 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is fair (2/5), and weldability is poor (1/5). Typical applications include: Cold-work tooling, blanking dies, forming dies, slitter knives, thread rolling dies, shear blades, punches. Key engineering considerations: Brittle in hardened condition. Very low elongation - cannot deform. Must be machined before hardening. Susceptible to fracture under impact load.

weldability_notes: Welding generally avoided. Requires full re-heat treatment after welding.
typical_applications: Air-hardening tool steel for dies, punches, gauges, forming rolls, woodworking tools, master tools.
key_warnings: Brittle when hardened. Air hardening means minimal distortion - useful for complex shapes. Lower wear resistance than D2 but better toughness.
description_text: Tool Steel A2 (Hardened & Tempered) is a tool steel with a yield strength of 1620 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is poor (1/5). Typical applications include: Air-hardening tool steel for dies, punches, gauges, forming rolls, woodworking tools, master tools. Key engineering considerations: Brittle when hardened. Air hardening means minimal distortion - useful for complex shapes. Lower wear resistance than D2 but better toughness.

weldability_notes: Welding generally avoided. If required full re-heat treatment after welding.
typical_applications: Die casting dies, hot forging dies, extrusion tooling, plastic injection molds, aluminum die casting.
key_warnings: Excellent hot toughness and thermal fatigue resistance. Must be pre-heated before use to avoid thermal shock cracking. Check hardness regularly in hot service.
description_text: Tool Steel H13 (Hot-Work Hardened) is a tool steel with a yield strength of 1200 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is poor (1/5). Typical applications include: Die casting dies, hot forging dies, extrusion tooling, plastic injection molds, aluminum die casting. Key engineering considerations: Excellent hot toughness and thermal fatigue resistance. Must be pre-heated before use to avoid thermal shock cracking.

weldability_notes: Excellent - TIG/MIG with ER1100 filler. No preheat. Highest weldability of all aluminums.
typical_applications: Sheet metal work, spun hollow parts, cooking utensils, chemical equipment, food packaging, decorative trim, heat exchangers.
key_warnings: Very low strength - not for structural applications. No true endurance limit. Work hardens rapidly. Good formability but poor strength is the tradeoff.
description_text: Aluminum 1100 (Annealed) is an aluminum wrought with a yield strength of 35 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: Sheet metal work, spun hollow parts, cooking utensils, chemical equipment, food packaging. Key engineering considerations: Very low strength - not for structural applications. No true endurance limit. Work hardens rapidly.

weldability_notes: Good weldability but HAZ softens back to annealed condition. Use ER1100 filler.
typical_applications: Sheet metal parts, fin stock, heat exchanger fins, packaging - where slightly higher strength than annealed is needed.
key_warnings: Cold work improves strength but reduces ductility. HAZ loses all cold-work strengthening. Same corrosion as 1100-O.
description_text: Aluminum 1100 (H14 Half-Hard) is an aluminum wrought with a yield strength of 120 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: Sheet metal parts, fin stock, heat exchanger fins, packaging. Key engineering considerations: Cold work improves strength but reduces ductility. HAZ loses all cold-work strengthening.

weldability_notes: Excellent - TIG/MIG with ER4043 or ER5356. No preheat. Excellent weldability.
typical_applications: Cooking utensils, chemical equipment, pressure vessels, sheet-metal work, builders hardware, storage tanks, radiators.
key_warnings: Low strength - not structural. Slightly stronger than 1100 due to manganese addition. No true endurance limit. Good formability and corrosion resistance.
description_text: Aluminum 3003 (Annealed) is an aluminum wrought with a yield strength of 40 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is excellent (5/5). Typical applications include: Cooking utensils, chemical equipment, pressure vessels, sheet-metal work, builders hardware, storage tanks, radiators. Key engineering considerations: Low strength - not structural. Slightly stronger than 1100 due to manganese addition. No true endurance limit.

weldability_notes: Not recommended for fusion welding - hot cracking. Use rivets or friction stir welding.
typical_applications: Aerospace structural, aircraft fuselage and wing skins, military equipment, truck wheels, high-stress fittings.
key_warnings: Almost always supplied clad (Alclad). Not weldable conventionally. No true endurance limit. SCC risk in transverse direction.
description_text: Aluminum 2024-T3 is an aluminum wrought with a yield strength of 345 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is poor (1/5). Typical applications include: Aerospace structural, aircraft fuselage and wing skins, military equipment, truck wheels, high-stress fittings. Key engineering considerations: Almost always supplied clad (Alclad). Not weldable conventionally. No true endurance limit. SCC risk in transverse direction.

weldability_notes: Excellent with TIG/MIG using ER5356 filler. No preheat. Avoid ER4043 - cracking risk.
typical_applications: Marine sheet metal, boat hulls, fuel tanks, pressure vessels, kitchen equipment, electronic enclosures, architectural panels.
key_warnings: No true endurance limit. Properties drop significantly above 150 C. SCC risk if held above 65 C for long periods after H32.
description_text: Aluminum 5052-H32 is an aluminum wrought with a yield strength of 186 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is good (4/5). Typical applications include: Marine sheet metal, boat hulls, fuel tanks, pressure vessels, kitchen equipment, electronic enclosures, architectural panels. Key engineering considerations: No true endurance limit. Properties drop significantly above 150 C. SCC risk if held above 65 C for long periods after H32.

weldability_notes: Good weldability with ER4043 or ER5356 filler. Loses T6 temper in heat-affected zone - 25-40% strength loss near weld.
typical_applications: Bicycle frames, structural extrusions, scaffolding, machine parts, marine fittings (non-immersed), automotive parts.
key_warnings: Most common general-purpose aluminum. Welding annealed HAZ reduces strength significantly. No true endurance limit. Not as marine-resistant as 5052.
description_text: Aluminum 6061-T6 is an aluminum wrought with a yield strength of 276 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is moderate (3/5), and weldability is good (4/5). Typical applications include: Bicycle frames, structural extrusions, scaffolding, machine parts, marine fittings (non-immersed), automotive parts. Key engineering considerations: Most common general-purpose aluminum. Welding annealed HAZ reduces strength significantly. No true endurance limit. Not as marine-resistant as 5052.

weldability_notes: Essentially not weldable - severe hot cracking. Mechanical fasteners only.
typical_applications: Aircraft structural components (wing spars, fuselage frames), high-stress aerospace parts, bicycle frames (high-end), defense parts.
key_warnings: Highest strength common aluminum. Cannot be welded. Severe SCC risk in T6 - use T73 or T76 if SCC exposure. Poor corrosion - must be Alclad or coated.
description_text: Aluminum 7075-T6 is an aluminum wrought with a yield strength of 503 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is poor (1/5). Typical applications include: Aircraft structural components (wing spars, fuselage frames), high-stress aerospace parts, bicycle frames (high-end), defense parts. Key engineering considerations: Highest strength common aluminum. Cannot be welded. Severe SCC risk in T6 - use T73 or T76 if SCC exposure. Poor corrosion - must be Alclad or coated.

weldability_notes: Weldable with ER4043 filler. Requires re-heat treatment for full strength.
typical_applications: Engine blocks, transmission housings, intake manifolds, automotive wheels (cast), pump housings, complex shaped parts.
key_warnings: Cast - porosity issues possible. Lower properties than wrought aluminum. Best for complex geometries that would be expensive to machine from wrought.
description_text: Aluminum 356.0-T6 (Cast) is an aluminum cast with a yield strength of 165 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is moderate (3/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Engine blocks, transmission housings, intake manifolds, automotive wheels (cast), pump housings, complex shaped parts. Key engineering considerations: Cast - porosity issues possible. Lower properties than wrought aluminum. Best for complex geometries that would be expensive to machine from wrought.

weldability_notes: Brazing and soldering preferred. TIG welding possible with silicon bronze filler. Heat-affected zone softens significantly.
typical_applications: Ammunition cases, plumbing fittings, electrical terminals, hardware, decorative parts, springs.
key_warnings: Susceptible to dezincification in stagnant water. SCC risk in ammonia environments. Cold work increases strength but reduces ductility.
description_text: Brass C26000 (Cartridge Brass, Half Hard) is a copper alloy with a yield strength of 310 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is moderate (3/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Ammunition cases, plumbing fittings, electrical terminals, hardware, decorative parts, springs. Key engineering considerations: Susceptible to dezincification in stagnant water. SCC risk in ammonia environments. Cold work increases strength but reduces ductility.

weldability_notes: Welding generally avoided due to lead content. Brazing and soldering work well.
typical_applications: Screw machine parts, fittings, valve bodies, gears, decorative hardware - the gold standard for high-volume machined brass parts.
key_warnings: Contains lead (3.5%) - regulations may restrict use in food/water (RoHS, drinking water). Dezincification in stagnant water. Best machinability of all common materials (reference 100).
description_text: Brass C36000 (Free-Cutting Brass) is a copper alloy with a yield strength of 310 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is moderate (3/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Screw machine parts, fittings, valve bodies, gears, decorative hardware. Key engineering considerations: Contains lead (3.5%) - regulations may restrict use in food/water (RoHS, drinking water). Dezincification in stagnant water. Best machinability of all common materials (reference 100).

weldability_notes: Brazing preferred. TIG with silicon bronze filler. Tin addition gives better seawater performance than regular brass.
typical_applications: Marine hardware, propeller shafts, marine fasteners, condenser plates, valve stems for marine service, heat exchanger tubes in seawater.
key_warnings: Tin addition (0.5-1.5%) significantly improves seawater corrosion resistance vs regular brass. Still vulnerable to dezincification - use inhibited grades for severe service. Galvanic corrosion couple with copper-nickel alloys.
description_text: Naval Brass C46400 is a copper alloy with a yield strength of 360 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Marine hardware, propeller shafts, marine fasteners, condenser plates, valve stems for marine service. Key engineering considerations: Tin addition (0.5-1.5%) significantly improves seawater corrosion resistance vs regular brass. Still vulnerable to dezincification. Galvanic corrosion couple with copper-nickel alloys.

weldability_notes: Brazing preferred. Welding rarely needed - usually cast to shape.
typical_applications: Plain bearings, bushings, sleeve bearings, thrust washers, pump components, gear blanks - the standard bearing material.
key_warnings: Excellent embeddability (can absorb hard particles without scoring shaft). Good antifriction properties. Compatible with most lubricants. Lead content (8%) restricts food/water applications.
description_text: Bearing Bronze C93200 is a copper alloy with a yield strength of 125 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Plain bearings, bushings, sleeve bearings, thrust washers, pump components, gear blanks. Key engineering considerations: Excellent embeddability. Good antifriction properties. Lead content (8%) restricts food/water applications.

weldability_notes: Good weldability by brazing and soldering. TIG possible with silicon bronze filler. Use low heat input.
typical_applications: Bellows, clutch disks, cotter pins, diaphragms, fasteners, wire brushes, chemical hardware, textile machinery springs.
key_warnings: Good fatigue resistance and spring properties. Excellent corrosion resistance in most environments. Tin addition improves strength over pure brass. No lead restriction issues.
description_text: Phosphor Bronze C51000 (5% Sn) is a copper alloy with a yield strength of 130 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Bellows, clutch disks, cotter pins, diaphragms, fasteners, wire brushes, chemical hardware, textile machinery springs. Key engineering considerations: Good fatigue resistance and spring properties. Excellent corrosion resistance in most environments.

weldability_notes: Brazing and soldering excellent. Fusion welding difficult due to high thermal conductivity - requires high heat input and inert atmosphere.
typical_applications: Electrical wire and bus bar, plumbing tube, heat exchangers, roofing, decorative architecture, electrical contacts.
key_warnings: Highest electrical conductivity of common engineering metals. Excellent thermal conductivity. Soft - work-hardens easily. Poor machinability when annealed - cold-drawn easier. Oxidizes to green patina outdoors.
description_text: Pure Copper C11000 (ETP, Annealed) is a copper alloy with a yield strength of 70 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Electrical wire and bus bar, plumbing tube, heat exchangers, roofing, decorative architecture, electrical contacts. Key engineering considerations: Highest electrical conductivity of common engineering metals. Excellent thermal conductivity. Soft - work-hardens easily. Poor machinability when annealed. Oxidizes to green patina outdoors.

weldability_notes: Weldable with care - preheat 200-300 C, use Ni-based electrodes (ENi-CI). Often best to braze instead. Avoid if possible.
typical_applications: Engine blocks, machine tool bases, brake rotors, manifolds, pump housings, valve bodies, large bedplates.
key_warnings: No useful tensile yield - brittle failure in tension. Excellent in compression. Outstanding vibration damping. Graphite flakes give machinability but also crack initiation sites. Avoid impact loading.
description_text: Gray Cast Iron Class 30 is a cast iron with a yield strength of 0 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is fair (2/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Engine blocks, machine tool bases, brake rotors, manifolds, pump housings, valve bodies, large bedplates. Key engineering considerations: No useful tensile yield - brittle failure in tension. Excellent in compression. Outstanding vibration damping. Graphite flakes give machinability but also crack initiation sites. Avoid impact loading.

weldability_notes: Weldable with Ni-based filler. Preheat 200-300 C, slow cooling. PWHT recommended for crack-prone areas.
typical_applications: Crankshafts, gears, pump bodies, valve housings, automotive suspension parts, pipe fittings - where cast iron strength and toughness both needed.
key_warnings: Spheroidal graphite gives much better tensile strength and ductility than gray iron. More expensive than gray iron but tougher. Excellent fatigue properties. Designation 65-45-12 = 65 ksi UTS, 45 ksi yield, 12% elongation.
description_text: Ductile Iron 65-45-12 is a cast iron with a yield strength of 310 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is fair (2/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Crankshafts, gears, pump bodies, valve housings, automotive suspension parts, pipe fittings. Key engineering considerations: Spheroidal graphite gives much better tensile strength and ductility than gray iron. More expensive than gray iron but tougher. Excellent fatigue properties.

weldability_notes: TIG with AZ61A or AZ92A filler. Preheat 150-200 C. Use inert gas shielding - Mg burns in air. Specialized process.
typical_applications: Aircraft internal structure, automotive parts, luggage, portable power tools, laptop housings, camera bodies - weight-critical applications.
key_warnings: Lightest structural engineering metal. Fire hazard as chips/powder - pyrophoric. Galvanic corrosion with steel and aluminum. Poor creep above 120 C. Strict storage and machining protocols required.
description_text: Magnesium AZ31B (Extruded) is a magnesium alloy with a yield strength of 200 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Aircraft internal structure, automotive parts, luggage, portable power tools, laptop housings, camera bodies. Key engineering considerations: Lightest structural engineering metal. Fire hazard as chips/powder - pyrophoric. Galvanic corrosion with steel and aluminum. Poor creep above 120 C.

weldability_notes: Welding difficult due to high alloy content. Preheat required. Use AZ92A filler. Limited applications only.
typical_applications: High-strength aerospace and automotive structural forgings, aircraft engine housings, transmission cases.
key_warnings: Highest strength of common magnesium wrought alloys. Fire hazard in machining. Galvanic corrosion severe with steel. Requires anodizing or coating for any moisture exposure.
description_text: Magnesium AZ80A (T5 Temper) is a magnesium alloy with a yield strength of 380 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is poor (1/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: High-strength aerospace and automotive structural forgings, aircraft engine housings, transmission cases. Key engineering considerations: Highest strength of common magnesium wrought alloys. Fire hazard in machining. Galvanic corrosion severe with steel.

weldability_notes: Excellent - TIG/MIG with Ni 200 filler. No preheat normally required.
typical_applications: Chemical and food processing industry; aerospace equipment; electronic parts; caustic soda handling; plating anodes.
key_warnings: Very expensive. Low strength limits structural use. Excellent corrosion in alkaline environments. Sensitive to sulfur embrittlement above 300 C.
description_text: Nickel 200 (Pure, Annealed) is a nickel alloy with a yield strength of 100 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is good (4/5). Typical applications include: Chemical and food processing, caustic soda handling, plating anodes. Key engineering considerations: Very expensive. Low strength limits structural use. Sensitive to sulfur embrittlement above 300 C.

weldability_notes: Weldable with Monel filler. PWHT recommended. Preheat for heavy sections.
typical_applications: Pump shafts; valve stems; springs; marine fasteners; oil well tools; doctor blades; marine propeller shafts.
key_warnings: SCC susceptible in HF acid. Age hardening can cause embrittlement if done incorrectly. Very expensive. Requires careful heat treatment control.
description_text: Monel K-500 (Age Hardened) is a nickel alloy with a yield strength of 750 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Pump shafts, valve stems, springs, marine fasteners, oil well tools. Key engineering considerations: SCC susceptible in HF acid. Age hardening can cause embrittlement if done incorrectly. Very expensive.

weldability_notes: Excellent weldability with Inconel 82/182 filler. No preheat normally required.
typical_applications: Gas-turbine parts; heat-treating equipment; electronic parts; nuclear reactors; chemical processing; furnace components.
key_warnings: Very expensive. SCC in high-temperature pure water environments (nuclear). Sensitization possible in weld HAZ. Avoid sulfur atmospheres above 700 C.
description_text: Inconel 600 (Annealed) is a nickel alloy with a yield strength of 210 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is good (4/5), and weldability is good (4/5). Typical applications include: Gas-turbine parts, heat-treating equipment, electronic parts, nuclear reactors, chemical processing, furnace components. Key engineering considerations: Very expensive. SCC in high-temperature pure water environments. Sensitization possible in weld HAZ.

weldability_notes: Excellent weldability with matching Hastelloy filler. No preheat. Low heat input recommended.
typical_applications: Chemical process equipment; flue gas desulfurization; pulp and paper; pharmaceutical reactors; marine exhaust systems.
key_warnings: Highest corrosion resistance of common engineering alloys. Extremely expensive. Very poor machinability - carbide tooling only. Requires strict weld procedure qualification.
description_text: Hastelloy C-4 (Solution Treated) is a nickel alloy with a yield strength of 400 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is good (4/5). Typical applications include: Chemical process equipment, flue gas desulfurization, pulp and paper, pharmaceutical reactors, marine exhaust systems. Key engineering considerations: Highest corrosion resistance of common engineering alloys. Extremely expensive. Very poor machinability - carbide tooling only.

weldability_notes: Excellent - TIG with pure Ti filler. Full argon shielding and back-purging mandatory. Atmosphere contamination embrittles.
typical_applications: Chemical plant vessels; heat exchangers; marine components; desalination equipment; surgical implants; architectural cladding.
key_warnings: Fire hazard as fine powder. Galvanic corrosion accelerates mating carbon steel. Excellent corrosion including seawater and many acids. Lower strength than Ti-6Al-4V but better formability.
description_text: Titanium CP Grade 2 (Commercially Pure) is a titanium alloy with a yield strength of 275 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is good (4/5). Typical applications include: Chemical plant vessels, heat exchangers, marine components, desalination equipment, surgical implants, architectural cladding. Key engineering considerations: Fire hazard as fine powder. Galvanic corrosion accelerates mating carbon steel. Excellent corrosion in seawater.

weldability_notes: Excellent weldability with inert gas shielding. TIG with argon required. Atmosphere contamination embrittles weld - back-purging essential.
typical_applications: Aerospace structural (60% of all titanium use); jet engine compressor parts; medical implants; marine equipment; high-performance sporting goods.
key_warnings: Very expensive vs steel/aluminum. Poor machinability - high heat causes work hardening and tool wear. Fire hazard in finely divided form. Galvanic corrosion will accelerate carbon steel mating parts. Cannot be welded without inert gas.
description_text: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, Annealed) is a titanium alloy with a yield strength of 880 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is moderate (3/5). Typical applications include: Aerospace structural, jet engine compressor parts, medical implants, marine equipment, high-performance sporting goods. Key engineering considerations: Very expensive vs steel/aluminum. Poor machinability. Fire hazard in finely divided form. Galvanic corrosion will accelerate carbon steel mating parts.

weldability_notes: Weldability reduced in aged condition - solution treat and re-age after welding for full properties. Full argon shielding mandatory.
typical_applications: High-strength aerospace fasteners; aerospace components; honeycomb panels; jet engine structural components.
key_warnings: Highest strength titanium alloy. Cannot be welded in aged condition without full re-treatment. Fire hazard in finely divided form. Very expensive. Poor machinability in aged condition.
description_text: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, Solution+Age) is a titanium alloy with a yield strength of 1100 MPa. Corrosion resistance in seawater is excellent (5/5), and weldability is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: High-strength aerospace fasteners, aerospace components, honeycomb panels, jet engine structural components. Key engineering considerations: Highest strength titanium alloy. Cannot be welded in aged condition without full re-treatment. Fire hazard in finely divided form. Very expensive.

weldability_notes: Ultrasonic or hot-plate welding. Solvent bonding with MEK or acetone. Excellent adhesive bonding.
typical_applications: Consumer electronics housings; automotive interior trim; appliance bodies; toys; pipe fittings; 3D printing filament.
key_warnings: Not UV stable - yellows and becomes brittle outdoors without UV stabilizer grade. Attacked by ketones, esters, and chlorinated solvents. Not for food contact without food-grade certification. Flammable.
description_text: ABS (General Purpose) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 40 MPa. Chemical resistance to solvents is poor (1/5). Weldability by ultrasonic or solvent bonding. Typical applications include: Consumer electronics housings, automotive interior trim, appliance bodies, toys. Key engineering considerations: Not UV stable. Attacked by ketones and chlorinated solvents. Not for food contact without certification.

weldability_notes: Ultrasonic or hot-plate welding. Solvent bonding with MEK or acetone.
typical_applications: Outdoor enclosures; garden equipment; automotive exterior trim; outdoor signage; electrical housings exposed to sunlight.
key_warnings: Better UV resistance than standard ABS but still not as good as ASA or PC. Slightly lower mechanical properties than general ABS. Same solvent sensitivity.
description_text: ABS (UV-Stabilized) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 38 MPa. Improved outdoor UV resistance vs standard ABS. Typical applications include: Outdoor enclosures, garden equipment, automotive exterior trim. Key engineering considerations: Better UV resistance than standard ABS but still limited. Same solvent sensitivity as standard ABS.

weldability_notes: Ultrasonic welding. Hot-plate welding. Adhesive bonding with epoxy or cyanoacrylate.
typical_applications: Gears; bearings; bushings; structural brackets; cable ties; automotive under-hood parts; conveyor components.
key_warnings: Absorbs moisture significantly (up to 8.5% at saturation) - strength and stiffness drop 30-40% when wet. Dry-as-molded properties are best-case. Attacked by strong acids and oxidizing agents. Swells in contact with some fuels.
description_text: Nylon 6/6 (PA66, Dry) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 83 MPa (dry). Chemical resistance to solvents is fair (2/5). Typical applications include: Gears, bearings, bushings, structural brackets, cable ties, automotive under-hood parts. Key engineering considerations: Absorbs moisture significantly - strength drops 30-40% when wet. Always specify wet or dry conditions for design.

weldability_notes: Ultrasonic welding. Hot-plate welding. Adhesive bonding.
typical_applications: Gears and bearings in humid environments; outdoor structural brackets; marine components; food processing parts.
key_warnings: These are equilibrium moisture-conditioned properties (50% RH) - more representative for most real-world applications than dry-as-molded. Use these values for design unless parts will be kept dry. Same chemical sensitivities as dry grade.
description_text: Nylon 6/6 (PA66, Moisture Conditioned) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 55 MPa (conditioned). More representative of real-world service than dry-as-molded values. Typical applications include: Gears and bearings in humid environments, outdoor structural brackets, marine components. Key engineering considerations: These are equilibrium moisture properties at 50% RH. Use these for design unless part is kept permanently dry.

weldability_notes: Ultrasonic welding. Solvent bonding with methylene chloride. Adhesive with epoxy.
typical_applications: Safety glasses lenses; machine guards; light covers; electronic enclosures; medical devices; CDs and DVDs; bulletproof glazing.
key_warnings: Outstanding impact resistance - virtually unbreakable. Attacked by strong alkalis, aromatic solvents, and ketones. UV degrades surface unless UV-stabilized grade used. Stress cracking risk with many chemicals. Not for continuous outdoor exposure without UV coating.
description_text: Polycarbonate (PC, General) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 62 MPa. Outstanding impact resistance. Typical applications include: Safety glasses lenses, machine guards, light covers, electronic enclosures, medical devices. Key engineering considerations: Outstanding impact resistance - virtually unbreakable. Attacked by strong alkalis and aromatic solvents. UV degrades surface without UV-stabilized grade.

weldability_notes: Hot-plate or butt welding. Electrofusion welding for pipe. Adhesive bonding difficult - requires surface treatment.
typical_applications: Chemical storage tanks; cutting boards; pipe systems; playground equipment; marine dock fenders; food containers; geomembranes.
key_warnings: Excellent chemical resistance but very low strength. Cannot be bonded with standard adhesives without surface treatment (flame or corona). Creeps significantly under sustained load. Not for structural applications. UV grades available for outdoor use.
description_text: HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 26 MPa. Excellent chemical resistance (5/5 across most environments). Typical applications include: Chemical storage tanks, cutting boards, pipe systems, playground equipment, marine dock fenders. Key engineering considerations: Very low strength. Cannot be bonded with standard adhesives. Creeps under sustained load.

weldability_notes: Cannot be conventionally welded or bonded. Mechanical fastening or PTFE tape compression seals only.
typical_applications: Seals and gaskets; non-stick cookware coating; chemical pipe liners; electrical insulation; bearing pads; laboratory equipment; valve seats.
key_warnings: Outstanding chemical resistance to virtually all chemicals - one of few materials resistant to hydrofluoric acid. Cannot be injection molded - requires sintering. Extremely poor adhesion - nothing sticks to it. Cold-flows (creeps) under load. Expensive. Not for structural applications.
description_text: PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 14 MPa. Outstanding chemical resistance to virtually all chemicals. Typical applications include: Seals and gaskets, chemical pipe liners, electrical insulation, bearing pads, laboratory equipment. Key engineering considerations: Outstanding chemical resistance. Cannot be welded or bonded. Cold-flows under load. Cannot be injection molded.

weldability_notes: Ultrasonic welding. Hot-plate welding. Adhesive bonding difficult.
typical_applications: Precision gears; bearings; bushings; fasteners; plumbing fittings; pump components; door handles; zippers; fuel system parts.
key_warnings: Excellent dimensional stability and low friction - the go-to plastic for precision mechanical parts. Attacked by strong acids and oxidizing agents. Degrades near open flames - produces formaldehyde gas. Not for contact with strong acids. Two types: homopolymer (Delrin - better strength) and copolymer (better chemical resistance, easier to machine).
description_text: POM / Acetal (Delrin) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 68 MPa. Excellent dimensional stability and low friction. Typical applications include: Precision gears, bearings, bushings, fasteners, plumbing fittings, pump components. Key engineering considerations: Excellent dimensional stability and low friction. Attacked by strong acids. Degrades near open flames producing formaldehyde gas.

weldability_notes: Hot-plate welding. Ultrasonic welding (requires special tooling). Difficult to adhesive bond.
typical_applications: Food containers; medical syringes; automotive battery cases; living hinges; rope; packaging; laboratory ware; chemical tanks.
key_warnings: Outstanding chemical resistance and lowest density of common plastics. Brittle below -10 C - use copolymer for cold environments. Fatigue-resistant for living hinges. UV degrades without stabilizer. Poor adhesion - difficult to bond. Not for hot water above 100 C.
description_text: Polypropylene (PP, Homopolymer) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 35 MPa. Lowest density of common structural plastics. Typical applications include: Food containers, medical syringes, automotive battery cases, living hinges, rope, packaging. Key engineering considerations: Outstanding chemical resistance. Brittle below -10 C. UV degrades without stabilizer. Poor adhesion.

weldability_notes: Solvent cementing with THF-based cement. Hot-gas welding. Ultrasonic welding.
typical_applications: Drainage and water supply pipe; window frames; cable insulation; chemical tanks; gutters; siding; conduit.
key_warnings: Releases toxic HCl gas when burned or overheated - handle with care during processing. Attacked by THF, ketones, and aromatic solvents. Becomes brittle at low temperatures. Softens above 60 C. Excellent flame resistance (self-extinguishing). Do not use near open flames or high heat sources.
description_text: PVC (Rigid, uPVC) is a plastic_thermoplastic with a yield strength of 55 MPa. Excellent flame resistance - self-extinguishing. Typical applications include: Drainage and water supply pipe, window frames, cable insulation, chemical tanks, gutters, siding. Key engineering considerations: Releases toxic HCl gas when burned. Attacked by ketones and aromatic solvents. Becomes brittle at low temperatures.

weldability_notes: Cannot be welded. Adhesive bonding excellent - epoxy bonds to almost everything. Mechanical fastening.
typical_applications: Adhesives; electrical potting and encapsulation; tooling and molds; coatings; printed circuit boards; composite matrix resin.
key_warnings: Brittle - low impact resistance. Cannot be re-melted or reformed after curing. Mix ratio and cure temperature critical for full properties. Some formulations require elevated temperature post-cure. Skin sensitizer - use PPE during mixing.
description_text: Epoxy Resin (Cast, Unfilled) is a plastic_thermoset with a yield strength of 60 MPa. Excellent adhesive bonding to most substrates. Typical applications include: Adhesives, electrical potting and encapsulation, tooling and molds, coatings, PCBs, composite matrix resin. Key engineering considerations: Brittle - low impact resistance. Cannot be re-melted. Mix ratio and cure temperature critical. Skin sensitizer.

weldability_notes: Cannot be welded or solvent bonded. Adhesive bonding with epoxy. Mechanical fastening.
typical_applications: Electrical insulators; circuit breakers; handles and knobs; brake linings; distributor caps; cookware handles.
key_warnings: Oldest synthetic plastic. Very brittle - low impact resistance. High hardness and good dimensional stability. Cannot be thermally recycled. Requires compression molding - not injection moldable in most formulations. Good heat resistance but chars rather than melts.
description_text: Phenolic (Bakelite) is a plastic_thermoset with a yield strength of 55 MPa. Excellent electrical insulation and heat resistance. Typical applications include: Electrical insulators, circuit breakers, handles and knobs, brake linings, distributor caps. Key engineering considerations: Very brittle. Cannot be thermally recycled. Requires compression molding. Good heat resistance but chars rather than melts.

weldability_notes: Cannot be welded. Brazing with active metal brazes possible. Mechanical fastening with care - brittle.
typical_applications: Wear-resistant components; electrical insulators; cutting tool substrates; thermocouple protection tubes; pump seals; spark plug bodies; grinding media.
key_warnings: Extremely brittle - zero ductility. Fails catastrophically in tension. Design for compression loading. Cannot be machined after sintering except by diamond grinding. Thermal shock sensitive - avoid rapid temperature changes. Outstanding wear and corrosion resistance.
description_text: Alumina Al2O3 (96% purity) is a ceramic_oxide with a flexural strength of 300 MPa. Outstanding wear resistance, hardness, and electrical insulation. Typical applications include: Wear-resistant components, electrical insulators, cutting tool substrates, pump seals, spark plug bodies. Key engineering considerations: Extremely brittle - zero ductility. Design for compression. Cannot be machined after sintering except by diamond grinding. Thermal shock sensitive.

weldability_notes: Cannot be welded. Brazing with active metal brazes. Mechanical fastening only.
typical_applications: Mechanical seals; pump faces; abrasive jet nozzles; kiln furniture; heat exchangers at extreme temperature; semiconductor processing.
key_warnings: Hardest common engineering ceramic. Extremely brittle - zero ductility. Best ceramic for combined high temperature and chemical resistance. More thermal shock resistant than alumina. Very expensive and difficult to machine - diamond tooling only. Not for applications with high tensile or impact loads.
description_text: Silicon Carbide (Sintered SiC) is a ceramic_carbide with a flexural strength of 400 MPa. Outstanding hardness, wear resistance, and high-temperature stability. Typical applications include: Mechanical seals, pump faces, abrasive jet nozzles, kiln furniture, heat exchangers at extreme temperature. Key engineering considerations: Hardest common engineering ceramic. Extremely brittle. Very expensive and difficult to machine - diamond tooling only.

weldability_notes: Cannot be conventionally welded or bonded. Flame working possible. Epoxy adhesive bonding.
typical_applications: Laboratory glassware; sight glasses; pharmaceutical packaging; telescope mirrors; cooking vessels; chemical reaction vessels.
key_warnings: Brittle - zero ductility. Stress concentrations from scratches or chips cause sudden failure. Low thermal expansion gives good thermal shock resistance vs soda-lime glass. Not for applications with tensile stress or impact. Handle with care. Inspect for chips before pressurizing.
description_text: Borosilicate Glass (Pyrex type) is a ceramic_glass with a flexural strength of 70 MPa. Good thermal shock resistance and excellent chemical resistance. Typical applications include: Laboratory glassware, sight glasses, pharmaceutical packaging, telescope mirrors, cooking vessels. Key engineering considerations: Brittle - zero ductility. Stress concentrations from scratches cause sudden failure. Not for applications with tensile stress or impact.

weldability_notes: Cannot be welded. Mechanical fastening (requires metal inserts or close-tolerance holes). Adhesive bonding with structural epoxy.
typical_applications: Aerospace structural panels; racing car monocoques; bicycle frames; wind turbine blades; pressure vessels; sports equipment.
key_warnings: Properties are highly directional - 0 degree values shown. Transverse (90 deg) strength is only ~50 MPa. Must design layup for multi-directional loading. Galvanic corrosion with aluminium - must isolate. Catastrophic brittle failure with no warning. Difficult and expensive to repair. Dust from cutting is a health hazard.
description_text: CFRP (Carbon Fibre, Unidirectional) is a composite_cfrp with a tensile strength of 1600 MPa (0 degree). Highest specific strength and stiffness of common engineering materials. Typical applications include: Aerospace structural panels, racing car monocoques, bicycle frames, wind turbine blades. Key engineering considerations: Highly directional - design layup carefully. Galvanic corrosion with aluminium. Catastrophic brittle failure. Expensive.

weldability_notes: Cannot be welded. Mechanical fastening with metal inserts. Adhesive bonding with structural epoxy.
typical_applications: Structural panels with multi-directional loading; aircraft skins; automotive body panels; industrial enclosures; sporting goods.
key_warnings: Quasi-isotropic layup (0/45/90/-45) gives near-equal properties in all in-plane directions. Lower properties than unidirectional but more practical for general loading. Same galvanic corrosion risk with aluminium. Delamination is the primary failure mode - avoid peel forces.
description_text: CFRP (Carbon Fibre, Quasi-Isotropic) is a composite_cfrp with a tensile strength of 600 MPa. Near-equal in-plane properties from (0/45/90/-45) layup. Typical applications include: Structural panels, aircraft skins, automotive body panels, industrial enclosures. Key engineering considerations: Lower than UD but more practical for general loading. Same galvanic corrosion risk with aluminium. Delamination is primary failure mode.

weldability_notes: Cannot be welded. Mechanical fastening. Adhesive bonding with structural epoxy or polyester.
typical_applications: Boat hulls; wind turbine blades; automotive body panels; chemical storage tanks; ladder rails; electrical enclosures; architectural panels.
key_warnings: Much lower cost than CFRP. Electrically non-conductive - ideal for electrical applications. No galvanic corrosion risk. Lower stiffness and strength than CFRP but adequate for many applications. Resin matrix limits max temperature. Glass fibres cause skin irritation during cutting - wear PPE. UV degrades resin surface over time.
description_text: GFRP (E-Glass Fibre, Woven Epoxy) is a composite_gfrp with a tensile strength of 300 MPa. Good strength-to-weight ratio at much lower cost than CFRP. Typical applications include: Boat hulls, wind turbine blades, automotive body panels, chemical storage tanks, ladder rails, electrical enclosures. Key engineering considerations: Much lower cost than CFRP. Electrically non-conductive. No galvanic corrosion risk. Resin matrix limits max temperature.

weldability_notes: Cannot be welded. Mechanical fastening. Adhesive bonding with structural epoxy.
typical_applications: Ballistic protection (body armour); pressure vessels; racing car safety structures; boat hulls; sports helmets; cut-resistant gloves.
key_warnings: Outstanding toughness and impact resistance - energy absorbing. Very difficult to cut - requires special scissors or diamond blade. Poor compression strength - do not use as primary compression member. Absorbs moisture - moisture degrades properties slightly. Fibres are difficult to machine cleanly.
description_text: Kevlar / Aramid Composite (Woven, Epoxy) is a composite_kevlar with a tensile strength of 500 MPa. Outstanding impact resistance and energy absorption. Typical applications include: Ballistic protection, pressure vessels, racing car safety structures, boat hulls, sports helmets. Key engineering considerations: Outstanding toughness. Very difficult to cut. Poor compression strength. Absorbs moisture slightly.
